context.process_name: Subsequent Closes: Equalization Interest & Investor Rebalance
context.objective: Document how we carry out Subsequent Closes: Equalization Interest & Investor Rebalance, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: What starts this work?

It kicks off when new money comes into a fund that has already been going for a while. So either a brand new investor gets let in, or somebody who is already in the fund decides to put in more. At that point we sort of true everyone up so the newcomer is on the same footing as the people who were there from the start.
Talk me through how you handle the equalization and rebalance once a new or additional investment comes in?

Sure, roughly speaking. We open up the close and make sure the investor is actually ready to come in. Then we pin down what the fund's partnership agreement says about how the catch-up is supposed to work, because it is different fund to fund. After that we go back through the earlier capital calls and work out what the new investor would have put in if they had been there all along, and we put interest on top of that. We figure out how that interest gets shared among the investors who were already in. Then a call goes out to the new investor for the catch-up amount. Once that is done we redo everybody's percentages going forward, and at the end we update the books and reconcile everything so the close can be shut.
What information from the earlier calls and the partnership agreement determines the catch-up and interest amounts?

From the earlier calls we need every capital call that happened before the investor's admission or effective date, and for each one the call date, the total base, what it was for, and how much each existing investor funded. From the partnership agreement, the LPA, plus any side letters, we take which part of each earlier call counts, the interest rate, the start and end dates, the day-count and accrual basis, whether it compounds, and who the interest goes to and how it is treated. The catch-up capital itself is the investor's approved commitment percentage times the included amount of each prior call, after any exclusions the fund's documents require. Interest then runs on each of those, call by call, from the original funding date to the admission or effective date. We never assume the day count, simple versus compound, or who receives it. That all has to come from the LPA.
How do you check that the catch-up and interest calculations are correct before the call goes out?
Mostly a second person goes over it, and we make sure the numbers all tie out before anything goes out the door. If something does not tie, the call just does not get released until it is sorted.
What do you compare the calculated amounts against when you tie them out?

A few things. The list of earlier calls and what each investor funded gets reconciled to the prior notices, the historical contribution records, the general ledger and trial balance, and the capital accounts, and there has to be zero unexplained difference. For the catch-up capital, the call-by-call detail has to add up to the total, and the percentage and the call base have to trace back to the executed commitments and approved inputs. For interest, the second reviewer independently recalculates it and checks the dates, rate, basis, compounding, formula and total against the method in the LPA. The interest we allocate out to the existing investors has to equal the total interest, with no leftover. And the notice itself, meaning the backdated capital, interest, fee and total due on it, has to agree to the approved schedules before it is released.
How do you determine each existing investor’s share of the interest?

It depends on the fund. I identify which existing investors are entitled to be compensated and the allocation basis the LPA sets, and then allocate the interest investor by investor on that basis. Then I apply whatever treatment the LPA requires, which can be a cash payment to them, an addition to their capital accounts, or some other approved mechanism. If any investor is excluded or gets special treatment, I document why. If it is unclear who should receive the interest, or whether it is cash or capital, I escalate it and the client or their legal counsel decides. I do not pick one myself. I could not give you one formula that works for every fund. There is supposed to be a fund-by-fund register of those LPA rules, but I do not know where that stands. Someone on the legal or governing-documents side would have to confirm it.
When you say “once that is done,” what has happened with the catch-up call?

By that point the call has been put together and sent. I assemble the new investor's backdated capital, the equalization interest, the management-fee catch-up if one applies, and any other approved component. I populate the allocation and notice data, and the notice shows each component separately plus the total due. It goes through internal review and the client approves it, and that part runs through our regular capital call process, which we call FA-01. The FA-01 team is the one that actually releases the notice. After that the funding is tracked through the cash application process, FA-02. The receipts themselves get reconciled at the very end, when we close out.
How do you recalculate each investor’s going-forward percentage after the new or additional commitment is included?

I recalculate the fund's total commitments after the close, using the executed post-close commitments, and then work out each investor's percentage of that for future events. I do not just reuse the old percentages sitting in Excel. I recalculate both the pre-close and the post-close totals. Where earlier investments keep different economics, which happens in deal-by-deal funds, I leave those investment-specific historical percentages as they are and do not overwrite them. Every schedule gets its effective date recorded. All of that lives in the commitment and ownership schedule and the Excel allocation engine. Then I update the inputs for future capital calls, distributions, the waterfall and reporting. The percentages have to reconcile to the approved commitments and add up to the required total, apart from documented exclusions or rounding, and the second reviewer has to approve them before the next event.
What tells you the investor is ready to be included in the close?

A few things have to be in place. I need the client's close notification and the executed subscription document, or the commitment-increase paperwork if it is an existing investor putting in more, and onboarding and the anti-money-laundering checks have to be finished. I confirm the client has approved the admission, that AML has cleared, and where the system and portal setup stands. I record it in the close checklist: the fund, the investor, the close or effective date, the commitment, and whether it is a new admission or an upsize. At the same time I assign a second reviewer, flag any legal, tax, management-fee or accounting dependencies, and set the completion date so it lands before the investor's next capital activity. If documents are incomplete, or the AML, commitment or effective-date records are missing, I escalate. No equalization call gets released for an investor who is not approved and cleared.
How does the close team learn that a new admission or commitment increase is coming?

Like I mentioned, it comes from the client. They send us a close notification, and the client is the one who confirms the admission date and the commitment. There is no fixed schedule for it. It is event-driven, and it can happen more than once while the fund is still fundraising. Investor Services is involved as well, since they confirm the onboarding, and they will hold the investor's participation or the notice if onboarding or the portal setup is not complete.
How does Investor Services let you know when onboarding and portal setup are complete so the hold can be lifted?
This capture still has open sections. 14 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.

steps.title: Receive close notification
steps.description: The client sends a close notification for a new admission or increased commitment in an established fund and confirms the admission date and commitment. The work is event-driven and may occur more than once during fundraising.

steps.title: Open the close
steps.description: Open the close to begin the investor true-up.

steps.title: Check investor readiness
steps.description: Confirm client admission approval, AML clearance and the status of system and portal setup. Required inputs include the client notification, executed subscription or commitment-increase paperwork, and completed onboarding and AML checks; Investor Services confirms onboarding.

steps.title: Identify catch-up rules
steps.description: Determine the catch-up rules from the fund’s LPA and any side letters. The participant says rules differ by fund and that day count, compounding and interest recipients must not be assumed.

steps.title: Calculate earlier-call catch-up
steps.description: For each call before admission or the effective date, apply the investor’s approved commitment percentage to the included amount after document-required exclusions. The participant needs each call’s date, total base, purpose and funding by each existing investor.

steps.title: Calculate catch-up interest
steps.description: Calculate interest call by call from the original funding date to the admission or effective date. Use the documented rate, date, day-count, accrual and compounding rules rather than assuming them.

steps.title: Allocate interest to investors
steps.description: Identify entitled existing investors and the LPA allocation basis, then allocate interest investor by investor. Document why an investor is excluded or receives special treatment; escalate uncertainty about recipients or treatment.

steps.title: Release catch-up notice
steps.description: The FA-01 team releases the notice after the reported checks, internal review and client notice approval. The investor must also be approved and AML-cleared; Investor Services may hold participation or the notice if onboarding or portal setup is incomplete.

steps.title: Recalculate investor percentages
steps.system: Commitment and ownership schedule; Excel allocation engine
steps.description: Recalculate pre-close and post-close commitment totals and each investor’s percentage for future events using executed post-close commitments, rather than reusing old Excel percentages. Preserve investment-specific historical percentages where earlier investments retain different economics, and record an effective date on every schedule.

steps.title: Update the books
steps.description: Update the books at the end of the work.

steps.title: Reconcile the close
steps.description: Reconcile everything at the end, including the receipts. Other items and reconciliation criteria are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Close ready to shut
steps.description: The books are updated and everything is reconciled so the close can be shut. Whether and how closure is recorded is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Review and tie out calculations

steps.description: Reconcile prior calls and investor funding to the stated records with no unexplained difference. Whether this is all or part of the reported internal review is UNKNOWN.

steps.description: The call is not released while a tie-out issue remains unresolved. How it is sorted and what happens immediately afterward are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Apply interest treatment
steps.description: Apply the LPA-required treatment after allocating interest. The participant reports possible cash payment, addition to capital accounts, or another approved mechanism.

steps.title: Escalate unclear interest rules
steps.description: Escalate uncertainty about who receives interest or whether its treatment is cash or capital. The participant does not choose the answer.

steps.title: Decide unclear interest treatment

steps.title: Track catch-up funding

topics.answer: The intake names the work Subsequent Closes: Equalization Interest & Investor Rebalance. It covers catch-up, interest allocation, a call, percentage rebalance and close-out. Other names for the overall work are UNKNOWN; FA-01 and FA-02 name connected procedures.

The participant describes truing investors up so the newcomer is on the same footing as investors present from the start, then updating percentages and books. The precise delivered close-out evidence and downstream recipient are UNKNOWN.

The client sends a notification for a new admission or an existing investor’s increased commitment and confirms date and commitment. It is event-driven, can recur during fundraising and has no fixed schedule. Receiver and channel are UNKNOWN. The participant sets a completion date before the investor’s next capital activity.

After the call is sent, percentages are recalculated. At the end books are updated and everything, including receipts, is reconciled so the close can be shut. The closure action, evidence, other reconciliation criteria and next consumer are UNKNOWN.

UNKNOWN: overall accountability was not identified. The participant performs several tasks, FA-01 releases notices, Investor Services confirms onboarding and a second reviewer approves percentages; these assignments do not establish overall accountability.

Open the close and check readiness; identify fund rules; calculate prior-call capital and interest; allocate interest and apply its treatment; assemble and release a reviewed, client-approved notice; recalculate percentages; update books and reconcile. The participant records a checklist and assigns a reviewer, Investor Services confirms onboarding, FA-01 releases and FA-02 tracks funding. Missing readiness items, unclear rules and failed tie-outs have escalation or hold paths, but their returns, several performers and exact handoffs remain UNKNOWN.

Prior calls and funding reconcile to notices, historical records, ledger, trial balance and capital accounts with zero unexplained difference. Catch-up detail and inputs are traced; a second reviewer independently recalculates interest; allocated interest and notice amounts tie to totals and approved schedules. An unresolved difference holds release. The client approves the notice, admission must be approved and AML-cleared, and a second reviewer approves percentages before the next event. Review order, other checks, evidence retention, rejection, rework and enforcement are UNKNOWN.

Fund documents determine included calls, interest and allocation; the participant reports cash, capital-account or other approved interest treatment. Deal-by-deal funds can retain investment-specific historical percentages. New admissions use subscriptions while upsizes use increase paperwork. Reasons beyond reported fund economics, boundary confirmation, incremental effort, charging and removal constraints are UNKNOWN.
UNKNOWN: the participant did not describe time-consuming work, errors, chasing or practical friction.
UNKNOWN: concrete failure consequences were not described. Reported holds and reconciliations do not establish a stated consequence or control effectiveness.

The participant mentions LPAs, side letters, prior notices, executed commitments, approved schedules and a close checklist. A fund-by-fund LPA rule register is supposed to exist, but its status is UNKNOWN. No documents were supplied or reviewed; locations and availability are largely UNKNOWN.

The work concerns established funds admitting a new investor or accepting an increased commitment. Rules vary by fund, including historical economics in deal-by-deal funds. Notice release runs through FA-01 and funding tracking through FA-02. General GPFS versus client-specific applicability, overall parent boundary and basis for any standard are UNKNOWN.

The participant reports that the LPA and side letters provide inclusion, rate, dates, accrual, compounding, recipient and treatment rules. Catch-up is the approved commitment percentage times included prior-call amounts after exclusions; interest runs call by call from funding to admission or effective date. Unclear recipients or cash/capital treatment go to the client or legal counsel. Other interpretation, conflicts, calculation location, rounding and corrections remain UNKNOWN; documents were not reviewed.

Client notification, executed investor paperwork and completed onboarding and AML are inputs. Investor Services confirms onboarding and can hold participation or the notice. FA-01 handles notice release; FA-02 tracks funding; future capital calls, distributions, waterfall and reporting use updated inputs. Exact handoffs, readiness signals and other dependencies are UNKNOWN.

Prior notices, contribution records, ledger, trial balance and capital accounts support reconciliation; executed commitments and approved inputs support calculations.
